# PREREG — does the public carry class c([d]G) stratify the isotypic trace ℓ(d) into within-class affine structure?

**Generated by `experiment-designer` (context-isolated), 2026-08-17.** Tests intersection γ of

when it cannot fire).

```
================================================================================
PREREG_isotypic_trace_carry_stratify_v1        FROZEN 2026-08-17
Test: does the public carry class c([d]G) stratify the isotypic trace ℓ(d)
into within-class AFFINE structure that ℓ lacks globally?
Scope lock: p=43 ONLY. A_new order 1893=3·631, λ=25. 15 rational-lift d.
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. FROZEN STRUCTURE REPORT  — compute and PRINT these BEFORE any fit or shuffle.
   Every downstream number inherits and must cite these. No fit runs until §0
   is printed. (This is the analogue of "report per-class counts first".)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
FS1  Per-carry-class POINT counts (n0, n+, n−), Σ = 15.
FS2  GLV-orbit decomposition of the 15 d. Orbit of scalar d = {d, 25d, 625d}
     mod 1893, intersected with the table. List each orbit and its size
     ∈ {1,2,3}. M := number of distinct orbits present. Report the multiset of
     orbit sizes (how many triples / pairs / singletons).
     [RUN CLARIFICATION, disclosed pre-data: the scalar d lives mod nE=31 (the
      order of G), not mod 1893 (where ℓ lives); the orbit is {d,25d,625d} mod
      nE=31. λ=25 has order 3 mod 31. This is the obvious intent; recorded so it
      is not a silent change.]
FS3  Per-carry-class ORBIT counts (m0, m+, m−), Σ = M. Carry is established as
     orbit-invariant, so this is well-defined — but VERIFY it (FS5) first.
FS4  N_perm := M! / (m0! · m+! · m−!)  (number of DISTINCT orbit→class
     partitions of the given sizes). This is the exact size of the matched null.
FS5  INTEGRITY CHECKS (both must pass or the test is invalid — branch B0):
     (a) No orbit spans two carry classes  (carry orbit-invariance holds on the
         actual table).
     (b) For every present orbit member d' = 25^t · rep, ℓ(d') ≡ k^t · ℓ(rep)
         mod 1893 with a single k ∈ {1849,587} per orbit (orbit-covariance holds
         on the actual table). t is the ×25 exponent taking rep→d'.
     A failure here means the stated ESTABLISHED facts are contradicted by the
     table itself → do NOT infer; flag and stop (B0).

REDUCED DATASET (the object the test runs on):
     For each orbit j, rep_j := the SMALLEST d in that orbit present in the
     table (frozen tie-rule). Row_j := (rep_j, e_j, c_j) where e_j := ℓ(rep_j)
     ∈ Z/1893 and c_j := carry class of the orbit. There are exactly M rows.
     The non-rep members are DROPPED: they are k^t·e_j by FS5(b) and carry no
     information beyond the orbit label. Dropping them is what removes the
     KNOWN orbit-covariance so the OPEN question (partial-d info beyond the
     orbit label) is what remains. Affine-in-d is not orbit-invariant (ℓ scales
     by k along the orbit), so the rep=min-d rule is part of the frozen
     hypothesis and is disclosed as such.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. OBJECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The map orbit-rep ↦ (e_j, c_j): for each GLV orbit present, its canonical trace
scalar e_j = ℓ(rep_j) ∈ Z/1893 and its public carry class c_j ∈ {0,+,−}. We
test whether, PARTITIONED BY c, the M points {(rep_j, e_j)} lie on a per-class
affine line e ≡ a_c·rep + b_c (mod 1893) more than a size-matched random
partition would. Feature (carry c) and target (ℓ) are constructed from disjoint
data — c from the x-coordinate Eisenstein lift, ℓ from an A_new dlog — so this
is NOT a shared-construction tautology. The one tautology that IS present, the
orbit-covariance ℓ(λd)=kℓ(d), is removed by the orbit-rep reduction in §0.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. STATISTIC   (exactly one primary; component readouts are secondary)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Affine-in-Z/1893 ⇔ collinearity ⇔ vanishing 2×2 determinant. Because
Z/1893 ≅ F_3 × F_631 (product of FIELDS), det≡0 mod 1893 ⇔ (a_c,b_c) exists
mod 1893 by CRT, so the determinant test is EXACTLY the affine-existence test —
no ring-search, no zero-divisor ambiguity.

For an ordered triple of rows (i,j,l):
   Det(i,j,l) := (rep_j−rep_i)(e_l−e_i) − (rep_l−rep_i)(e_j−e_i)  mod 1893.
Triple is collinear (affine-consistent) ⇔ Det ≡ 0.

PRIMARY STATISTIC (integer, no fit, no search, no float):
   T  :=  Σ_{c ∈ {0,+,−}}  #{ {i,j,l} ⊆ (orbit-reps of class c) : Det ≢ 0 }
        = total count of NON-collinear within-carry-class rep-triples.
   Lower T = more within-class affine structure. Classes with ≤2 reps have zero
   triples and contribute 0 to T — the small-sample FORCED cells contribute
   nothing (see §2-FORCEDNESS). T ranges 0 … Σ_c C(m_c,3).

Why this is not the rejected "fit-affine-and-count-successes" statistic:
T's absolute value is never interpreted. Only its RANK inside the matched
permutation null (§3) is read. A statistic that fit a≤3-point affine line and
counted hits would be upward-biased; here the SAME bias is present under every
permutation, so it cancels in the rank. See §2-FORCEDNESS.

PRE-REGISTERED COMPONENT READOUTS (guard the "effect lives in a subspace"
failure mode; reported alongside, do NOT change the primary verdict):
   T_3   := same count with Det taken mod 3   (F_3 factor).
   T_631 := same count with Det taken mod 631 (F_631 factor).
An affine effect localized to one CRT factor (mod-631 signal under mod-3 noise,
or vice versa) is invisible to full-1893 T but visible here. NOTE: T_3 has only
3 residues, so ~1/3 of triples are collinear by chance → low resolution / high
false-positive; the informative factor is T_631. Both carried at Bonferroni
α = 0.05/2 = 0.025 as EXPLORATORY leads, never as the primary verdict.

2-FORCEDNESS (the overfit audit, stated now):
 • A class with m_c ≤ 2 reps: C(m_c,3)=0 triples → contributes 0 to T under the
   true labels AND under every permutation → cannot bias the rank. Forced cells
   are inert, not positive.
 • The real signal lives only in classes with m_c ≥ 3, where the affine model
   (2 params) has residual DOF = m_c − 2 ≥ 1. A within-class affine claim is
   never emitted for a class with m_c < 3.
 • If NO class has m_c ≥ 3, T is constant across the null (=0 everywhere) →
   zero power → the planted control (§4) cannot fire → ABSTAIN (B1).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. MATCHED CONTROL  (the null)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Permute the carry LABELS over the M ORBIT-REPS, preserving the exact per-class
orbit counts (m0,m+,m−). Recompute T. Exact permutation null over all N_perm
distinct partitions (or, if N_perm is large, a fixed frozen random sample of
100000 partitions drawn without replacement from the partition set; report which
mode was used and the sample size).
   p := #{ partitions π : T_π ≤ T_true } / N_perm     (identity included).
p is an exact integer ratio.

PRESERVES: orbit structure; orbit-covariance; every e_j and rep_j; per-class
orbit counts; and — crucially — the ORBIT-INVARIANCE of the label (one label per
orbit-rep, so shuffled labels are constant on orbits, exactly as real carry is).
DESTROYS: only the specific assignment of which orbits share a carry class.

WHY POINT-LEVEL SHUFFLE IS BANNED (invalid null): permuting labels over the 15
POINTS would place orbit-mates in different classes, destroying the carry's
orbit-invariance — a symmetry real carry has BY DEFINITION. That is precisely
the "shuffle destroys a symmetry the readout has by definition" failure. We
shuffle at the ORBIT-REP level only.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. PLANTED / CALIBRATION CONTROLS  (must run every time, before verdict)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PLANTED-POSITIVE (graded), fires ⇒ test is powered:
   For corruption level f ∈ {0,1,2,3}: draw fixed per-class constants
   (A_c,B_c) from a DISCLOSED seed; set e'_j := A_{c_j}·rep_j + B_{c_j} mod 1893
   for every rep; then in the majority class corrupt f randomly-chosen reps by
   adding a fixed nonzero constant (seed-disclosed). Run §2–§3 on {e'_j}.
   • f=0 must give T'_true = 0 (perfect within-class affine) and, generically,
     p = 1/N_perm (only the true partition attains 0). The DETECTION BOUNDARY
     f* := largest f with p ≤ 0.05 is the reported power (§5).
   • If f=0 does NOT reach p ≤ 0.05, the statistic cannot detect even a perfect
     plant at these class sizes ⇒ the null is uninformative ⇒ ABSTAIN (B1).
     This is the single gate: it fires iff (some m_c ≥ 3) AND (N_perm ≥ 20).

CALIBRATION-NEGATIVE (carry-independent ℓ) must return NULL:
   Set e''_j := e_j but with carry labels replaced by one fixed random
   partition (seed-disclosed). Expected p ≈ 0.5 (T'' near the null median).
   If this returns p ≤ 0.05, the null is mis-implemented — halt and fix.

All plant/calibration constructions are exact over Z/1893; seeds are printed.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. POWER
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Minimum reachable p-value = 1/N_perm (FS4). The primary test is declared POWERED
iff BOTH:
   (P1) at least one class has m_c ≥ 3   (residual DOF ≥ 1), AND
   (P2) N_perm ≥ 20                       (so p ≤ 0.05 is attainable).
(P1∧P2) is exactly the condition under which the f=0 plant fires; the plant is
the operational power check.

Detectable effect size = the graded plant boundary f*: the test detects a within-
majority-class affine relation holding for all but ≤ f* of the m_big reps, at
p ≤ 0.05. Report f* as THE power number, with m_big and N_perm cited.

If (P1∧P2) fails: state plainly — underpowered at p=43 with these class sizes;
NO non-forced within-class test has power; ABSTAIN. A larger A_new is owed and
is currently BLOCKED (Sage/Singular hang above p=43); record it as owed, dated.

Secondary EXPLORATORY (affine-in-GLV-halves, 3 params): run ONLY on a class with
m_c ≥ 5 (residual DOF ≥ 2), same permutation null, Bonferroni-noted; otherwise
ABSTAIN-exploratory. Given the 3/4:1/8:1/8 law this will almost surely ABSTAIN;
it never affects the primary verdict.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. SCOPE  (absolute banner — every emitted number carries it)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
p = 43. This A_new (order 1893 = 3·631, λ = 25). These 15 rational-lift scalars
d only. NOTHING transfers to a larger A_new, to other p, or to secp256k1. A
positive is a LEAD to re-run the identical spec at a larger A_new — it is not a
result about any A_new other than this one.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. FALSIFICATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The stratification hypothesis is falsified AT THIS SCOPE if the test is powered
(P1∧P2, f=0 plant fires) and T_true is NOT in the low tail: p > 0.05. That is,
the true carry partition is no more within-class-affine than a size-matched
random partition. (Falsification is scoped: it does not close the partial-d-info
question — see anti-suppression note.)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. EXACTNESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Signal path is integer throughout: ℓ, e_j, carry c, Det (mod 1893 / 3 / 631),
all triple counts, N_perm, and every p-value (exact integer ratio). No float
enters the signal path and no float threshold decides any verdict. The
3/4:1/8:1/8 population law is analytic CONTEXT (used only to set expectations in
§0), never in the path. No float carve-out is required.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. PRE-COMMITMENT  (filled BEFORE the run; one branch per outcome)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
B0  FS5 integrity fails (orbit spans two classes, or covariance ≠ k^t):
    → the stated ESTABLISHED facts contradict the table. FLAG, do not infer,
      ABSTAIN-with-flag. Resolve the table before any stratification claim.

B1  Not powered: f=0 plant does NOT reach p ≤ 0.05 (⇔ no class m_c≥3, or
    N_perm < 20):
    → ABSTAIN — underpowered at p=43 with these class sizes. This is NOT a null

B2  Powered AND primary p ≤ 0.05:
    → SCOPED POSITIVE. The public carry class stratifies ℓ into within-class

B3  Powered AND primary p > 0.05:
    → SCOPED NULL. No within-carry-class affine stratification detectable at
      this scope and power (f*). Report T_true, exact p, f*, scope. Does NOT
      close whether ℓ carries partial-d info (anti-suppression note).

B3b Powered, primary p > 0.05, BUT component T_631 (or T_3) p ≤ 0.025:
    → primary SCOPED NULL as in B3, PLUS a component-localized EXPLORATORY lead
      (the affine effect may live in one CRT factor). Flag it, do not bury it;

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ANTI-SUPPRESSION NOTE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A scoped null (B3) is a scoped null: it says "not detectable as within-carry-
class affine, at p=43, at power f*", and does NOT close whether ℓ carries partial
d-information beyond the orbit label. ABSTAIN (B1) is a valid, non-closing
outcome — underpowered, not negative. Neither B1 nor B3 licenses "carry does not
handle ℓ" as a general statement; the object is open pending a larger A_new.
Structure, if present, could live in the F_631 factor (B3b), in a non-affine
complexity class not tested here, or below the resolution N_perm affords — none
of which a bound of magnitude "no low tail" rules out.
```
